topic: Carotid endarterectomy symptom to surgery time

audits.title: 649 Compliance of Carotid Endarterectomy Pathway at a Vascular Unit - a Regional Audit
audits.standard: Symptom onset to carotid endarterectomy within 14 days
audits.setting: Vascular unit at Bedford Hospital covering Bedford, Milton Keynes and Luton hospitals

cycle1.result: 57.5% delayed beyond 14 days: LDH 19 (55%), BHT 14 (50%), MKUH 9 (90%).

audits.other_findings: 41 (56%) had delayed referral to vascular team; 36 (49%) delays after referral; 8 (10%) had secondary events awaiting surgery.
audits.citation: Hakeem A, Najem M. 649 Compliance of Carotid Endarterectomy Pathway at a Vascular Unit - a Regional Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac269.534.

audits.title: WTP1.14 A Regional Audit of Carotid Endarterectomy Symptom to Surgery Target Times within the North-East of England
audits.standard: NICE: symptom onset to carotid endarterectomy within 14 days
audits.setting: Three vascular units in the North-East of England (Sunderland Royal, Freeman, James Cook), National Vascular Registry data

cycle1.result: 45.45% within 14 days (median 16 days, IQR 4–102); referral within 7 days of symptoms 69.70%; surgery within 7 days of referral 25.76% (median 11.5 days).

audits.other_findings: Delay from referral to surgery was the biggest delay; a questionnaire on barriers was sent to regional vascular consultants and registrars.
audits.citation: Sillito S, Stansby G, Dunlop P, Wong P. WTP1.14 A Regional Audit of Carotid Endarterectomy Symptom to Surgery Target Times within the North-East of England. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.156.

audits.title: TPTh 5.11 An Audit of Carotid Symptoms to Referral Time would be helpful in Developing the Carotid Pathway to Improve Timely Referrals
audits.standard: National standards (National Vascular Registry): surgery within 14 days and referral within 7 days of symptoms
audits.setting: Vascular unit, Cumberland Infirmary; patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy

cycle1.result: 60% had surgery within 14 days (national 49%); median symptom to surgery 13 days (national 14); 60% referred within 7 days (national 72%).

audits.other_findings: No post-operative deaths; adjusted stroke and death rate 2.5% vs national 1.9%; average stay two days.
audits.citation: Imteaz S, Al-Massarweh O, Eifell R. TPTh 5.11 An Audit of Carotid Symptoms to Referral Time would be helpful in Developing the Carotid Pathway to Improve Timely Referrals. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.478.

audits.title: Delay prior to expedited carotid endarterectomy: a prospective audit of practice.
audits.standard: Carotid endarterectomy within 14 days of index symptom
audits.setting: Fast-track pathway from TIA clinic, Leicester Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: 74/87 (85%) underwent CEA within 14 days; median delay 8 days; 10 (11%) had recurrent symptoms before surgery.

audits.other_findings: Main cause of delay was lack of planned weekend operating with specialist anaesthetic and theatre staff.
audits.citation: Ali M, Stephenson J, Naylor AR. Delay prior to expedited carotid endarterectomy: a prospective audit of practice. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2013;46(4):404-410. doi:10.1016/j.ejvs.2013.07.015. PMID: 23973275.

audits.title: Factors Associated with Hospital Dependent Delay to Carotid Endarterectomy in the Dutch Audit for Carotid Interventions.
audits.standard: Guideline: carotid endarterectomy within 14 days of index event
audits.setting: Dutch Audit for Carotid Interventions, nationwide mandatory registry

cycle1.result: Median time to CEA 11 days (IQR 8-14); 78% had CEA within 14 days of first hospital consultation.

audits.other_findings: Delay associated with younger age, previous CEA, ocular symptoms and indirect referral; hospital volume was not a factor.
audits.citation: Kuhrij LS, Meershoek AJA, Karthaus EG, Vahl AC, Hamming JF, Nederkoorn PJ, et al.. Factors Associated with Hospital Dependent Delay to Carotid Endarterectomy in the Dutch Audit for Carotid Interventions. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2019;58(4):495-501. doi:10.1016/j.ejvs.2019.05.015. PMID: 31395431.

audits.title: Reasons for Delayed Carotid Endarterectomy for Symptomatic Carotid Stenosis in Norway 2018-2019: A National Audit.
audits.standard: National and international guidelines: carotid endarterectomy within 14 days of the index event
audits.setting: National audit using the Norwegian Registry for Vascular Surgery (NORKAR), 14 vascular units (10 participated)

cycle1.result: 179 of 686 (26%) CEAs for symptomatic stenosis were delayed beyond 14 days; in the 120 audited delayed cases, doctor delay 54, patient delay 28, both 10, medical reason 23, travel abroad 5.

audits.other_findings: National proportion operated within 14 days rose from 65% in 2015 to 83% in 2020; information campaigns recommended to address patient delay.
audits.citation: Altreuther M, Sørlie CH, Hansen BS, Lyng C, Myhre K, Rabben T, et al.. Reasons for Delayed Carotid Endarterectomy for Symptomatic Carotid Stenosis in Norway 2018-2019: A National Audit. EJVES Vasc Forum. 2025;64:78-82. doi:10.1016/j.ejvsvf.2025.07.003. PMID: 41541072.

audits.title: Timeliness and outcomes of carotid endarterectomy for symptomatic carotid artery stenosis: a single centre audit.
audits.standard: Carotid endarterectomy within 48 hours to 14 days of symptoms

cycle1.result: Median symptom to surgery 9 days; 119 (69%) operated within 14 days.

audits.other_findings: No 30-day deaths, strokes or TIAs; in 53 delayed cases the main cause (32, 60%) was accessing surgery after vascular review.
audits.citation: Lim ETA, Laws PE, Beresford TP, Khanafer AMA, Roake JA. Timeliness and outcomes of carotid endarterectomy for symptomatic carotid artery stenosis: a single centre audit. ANZ J Surg. 2020;90(3):345-349. doi:10.1111/ans.15757. PMID: 32080950.
